body.p: Greedy woman. On some land, they say, people lived. These people had a daughter-in-law. This sister-in-law usually cooks for them. She cooks their food: she cooks meat, she cooks fish. When it boils, of course, they sit down to drink tea. Here she scoops out of the cauldron's contents she has boiled. She leaves a piece in the cauldron on purpose. She leaves some pike, she leaves some meat, if the meat is cooked. These people apparently lived poorly. One day, they are drinking tea, eating, her comrades she fed, she herself ate. I guess she wanted more. The rest of them are almost done. Suddenly she reached for the cauldron with her spoon. From there something, [whether] a piece of pike, [whether] a piece of fish, she fished out. They hear her say, "Oh, I found my needlework bag." Her comrades were heard saying, "Well, you found it, you eat it." She ate it. Another time again. She seemed to have boiled the meat. The meat was boiled, they sat down. That sister-in-law has the cauldron next to her all the time. She scooped out the meat, her comrades sat down, ate and drank tea. The bride keeps looking at the cauldron. One day she reached in there again with a spoon. Yeah, she fished for something, found something there, a piece of meat. They hear her say, "Oh, I found my sack!" Her comrades look at her, surprised, upset. They don't say anything, they just look at each other. Some woman was heard to say: "Well, you'll have to eat it." They ate this, drank tea. Finished. That's what their daughter-in-law was like. Yeah, those comrades of hers guessed that's what she was doing anyway. She must have been sneaky. One day her companions, since she does that - her food boiled, her meat boiled, her fish boiled - scooped it all out. Her comrades had secretly left some piece of her behind, and indeed her sackcloth was thrown there, thrown into the cauldron. Yes, again, as they ate, she reached for the cauldron with her spoon. Suddenly this daughter-in-law of theirs cried out, audibly saying, "Oh, here it is, I really found my sack." Yes, her comrades probably thought to themselves, "Serves you right! Why are you doing this? Daughter-in-law! What are you doing?" Now older women say, "That's why, daughter-in-law, a child should not be cunning. If you want to say something, you have to say it directly. And the thoughts shouldn't be bad." It's a tale older women tell their children. That's it.
